gaps.quote: defines the endpoint operator as the operator a network realises
gaps.note: Named only in a forward reference to a later page, with no link. The one-clause definition relies on 'intermediate frames' and 'cancelled', which the page never explains.

gaps.quote: so that the intermediate changes cancel and the net effect depends only on the endpoints
gaps.note: The claim that intermediate changes cancel and the net effect depends only on the endpoints is asserted, not shown, and the page does not give the mechanism.

gaps.term: stored array and logical array relation
gaps.quote: and the frame relates it to the logical array
gaps.note: The page announces an equation relating the stored array to the logical array, but the equation is missing, so the reader cannot tell how the stored array is computed from g.

gaps.quote: Along an edge the frame changes but the logical array does not
gaps.note: Stated without justification or formula. The reader cannot check why the logical array stays the same while the frame changes along an edge.

gaps.quote: so a route through the network changes only the endpoint frames
gaps.note: The conclusion that a route changes only the endpoint frames, and the reason the endpoint operator is defined in terms of them, does not follow from anything the page gives.
